newsitem.title: RUSSIA: RUSSIAN MINFINS MIXED, WATCH U.S. STATISTICS.
newsitem.headline: RUSSIAN MINFINS MIXED, WATCH U.S. STATISTICS.

text.p: Russian MinFin bonds were mixed in healthy volumes on Monday as a dip following a fall in U.S. Treasuries was compensated by short position covering, dealers said.
They forecast fluctuating prices in the next few days and said the market would be closely watching U.S. economic data to be released this week.
tranche Aug 11 Aug 8
"In the morning there was a dip linked to the drop in the price of U.S. Treasuries, but we are catching up now," said Eurobank dealer Olivier Coursault.
A Western bank dealer said the rise was due to covering of short positions created on Friday, when U.S. Treasuries fell.
He said the market was waiting for U.S. statistics.
"Now is the moment when the rally is over and evaluation of U.S. economy starts," he said.
The United States will announce its July Producer Price Index on Wednesday and Consumer Price Index on Thursday.
MinFin bonds, like other emerging market debt, are influenced by U.S. Treasury prices and so are sensitive to interest-rate news from the U.S.
The dealer forecast a flat market is the next few days.
"There will be buying, but not as crazy as last week," he said.
MinFins rose strongly in the last two weeks as Russia said it was making progress in reconciling its debt to the London Club of commercial bank-creditors.
Prices rose so high that some dealers said spreads over U.S. Treasuries had narrowed dangerously.
"I do not think there will be active buying," the Western dealer said. "The market is overheated. The market has overpriced the paper, there was no reason to fly so high up."
But Coursault said investors were still bullish on Russia.
Dealers said tranches 5, 6 and 7, the most volatile and cheap ones, were most actively traded.
--Julie Tolkacheva, Moscow Newsroom, +7095 941 8520
